summary: Develop the owner-chosen miniature-world carousel: three mechanics, three critics, one production script

final.title: Vous glissez. On construit. · La maquette qui se construit
final.one_liner: One locked camera watches a museum-grade scale model of a small street in the Algerian high plateaus. As the reader swipes, a bare plot becomes a finished shop whose window lights up with a homepage. The kickers mark the reader's three small moves (describe, send, decide) against everything the studio builds.
final.mechanics:
STATUS: this is a production plan only. Nothing is generated until the owner says go, because the user asked for planning and no generating yet.

1. WHAT WAS CHOSEN
- Base: 'La table de maquette', which all three critics ranked first. One square model tile, one locked frontal camera, a coded road on a straight street, coded joints at the seams, the gold drawing that becomes the building, and a coded end card.
- From 'Ici, bientôt…': the kickers À vous / À nous, the road's dash states as a progress meter, the coded homepage in the window, and the olive tree.
- From 'La rue qui se bâtit': the kraft-paper reveal, the light dip just before it, the tailor's-tape pun and the atlas loupe.
- From the critics: a steeper camera, keyframes first, plate lock (patch compositing) and short edit prompts.

2. CAMERA
- Every render uses one view: square-on, zero yaw, about 38° down, long telephoto.
- Zero yaw keeps the street a level horizontal line. The road can then be one straight coded line, and every overlay is plain 2D with no perspective maths (the drawing, brackets, dimension lines and the homepage in the window).
- 38° gives the high tabletop view that sells the miniature. At 32° the model read as an object on a shelf.

3. KEYFRAMES FIRST, NO FRAME DEEPER THAN TWO EDITS
Canva generate-image returns one image per call. Use PORTRAIT_4_5 for every scene frame and pass imageReferences by media id. Log every id.
- K0, the bare plate: text-to-image, depth 0. It is the cover.
- K1, the finished shop with a blank lit window: one edit of [K0], depth 1. It is slide 7.
- Additive in-betweens are edits of K0, with K1 as the footprint reference: F2 [K0, K1] and F3 [K0, K1].
- Subtractive and later frames are edits of K1: F4 [K1, K0], F5 [K1], F6 [K1, F5] and F8 [K1].
- Side assets, all SQUARE_1_1: the crate R1 [F4], and the loupe details D3 [F3] and D5 [F5].
- The cover is depth 0 and the payoff is depth 1, so the frames that matter most are the cleanest.

4. PLATE LOCK (patch compositing)
- Register every frame onto K0 with four anchors: the tile's two front-top corners and the front-top corners of both boundary walls. Use a similarity transform; the residual must be 4px or less.
- Use only each frame's plot patch. M_plot is a polygon between the inner faces of the two boundary walls, from the far curb up to y 440 in slide coordinates, feathered 20px.
- Outside M_plot, every slide shows K0's own pixels. S8 adds M_lamp (the lamp post, its head and its light pool, feathered 16px), because its lamp switches on.
- Match each patch's exposure to K0 with a CSS filter (brightness and contrast within ±6%), measured on the wall faces.
- Result: the street, sidewalks, walls, neighbours, tree, lamp, ridge and tile edges are pixel-identical from S1 to S8. The build is a true stop-motion, swiping back and forth replays it, and drift outside the plot no longer forces a re-roll.

5. NORMALISATION
- Measure one transform, T0, on K0 and apply it to every composited frame. It maps the tile's front-top corners to x 24 and x 1056, and the street centreline to y 1120.
- Allowed range: scale 0.9 to 1.1 and rotation of 1° or less. Outside that range, regenerate.
- Clip the image to x 24–1056.
- Opacity mask: 0 above y 440, rising to 1 at y 620. The ridge rises out of the dark under the type, and no text sits on the picture.
- Check on K1 that the top of the stair cube lands at y 660 or lower. If not, move the fade to 400–580 and keep every text block above y 540.

6. ONE STRIP
- Build the carousel in Claude Design as one 9720×1350 stage. Slide n is the 1080×1350 window at x (n−1)·1080.
- These layers are drawn once on the strip, so they cannot break at a seam:
  - the #0a1420 ground;
  - the Arcanum atmosphere: a teal glow top-left of S1, a brass crown top-right of S8–S9, and a brass lamp haze over each tile;
  - the brass grid: 64px, 1px rgba(230,180,80,.5) at .07, fading to 0 by y 620;
  - the tabletop band: void to navy #0f1e30 from y 1000 to 1250, back to void by 1350;
  - the table-edge hairline: 1px #27496b at y 1318;
  - the road.
- Each tile sits at x 24–1056 of its slide, so every seam is a 48px joint of coded tabletop between two model tiles. The renders never have to match each other across a seam.
- Each tile gets a coded contact shadow under its front face.

7. SEAM RIDER
- R1 is one closed, unmarked crate. Generate it on flat mid-grey (never navy on navy), remove the background in Canva, then grade it in code to the tile's light.
- It is about 180px wide, with its base on y 1120. It is centred on x 1080 of S3 and on x 0 of S4; each slide clips its own half, and the swipe joins them. It reads as your content in transit, carried across by your own thumb.

8. LIGHT LIVES IN CODE
- The renders never contain drawn light. These are all coded:
  - the gold drawing, traced once from K1 and reused at fixed coordinates: 100% with a pen-tip spark on S1, .45 on S2, .35 on S3, only the unbuilt parts at .30 on S4, and gone from S5;
  - the road, dimension lines, corner brackets and light pools;
  - the homepage in the window, mapped onto a frontal rectangle measured on K1.
- Practical lights are rendered: the window glow, the open door, the lantern and the street lamp. Only these switch on. The workshop lamp never changes, so nothing implies a day passing.

9. TYPE (Arcanum)
- Kicker at (54, 54): always a word, never a number.
- Headline: Cinzel 700, line height 1.03, .01em, in ice, with the closing words in crimson-text.
- Subline: Geist 400, 52px, line height 1.25, in body-strong.
- Every text block stays between x 54 and 1026 and ends above y 560.
- No page count, tile map, exit teaser or chevron. No glow, gradient or shadow on type.
- Widths were measured with the shipped woff2 faces (HarfBuzz, kerning on).

10. SELECTION AND QA
- For each frame:
  - inspect at 200% and reject any figure, hand, animal, vehicle, glyph or mark, glowing line, glass case, plinth or crane operator;
  - onion-skin the frame at 50% over K0 inside the plot: the footprint must sit where K1's shop stands, within 6px;
  - registration residual 4px or less.
- After composing:
  - check all eight seams on a 9720×1350 contact strip;
  - swipe through a private carousel preview on a phone;
  - check the glows for banding after export;
  - check the French spacing in every string.

11. EXPORT
- Export nine 1080×1350 sRGB PNGs (or JPEG at quality 95), uploaded in order, each with its French alt text.
- Bonus: the surroundings are plate-locked, so the eight frames make a 6–8 s stop-motion Reel with no new generation. It plays once and settles, and the carousel itself is its still version.

12. BUDGET
- 29 calls planned: K0 4, K1 4, F4 3, F6 3, F8 3, F2 2, F3 2, F5 2, R1 2, D3 2, D5 2.
- Plus about 9 re-rolls, so about 38 in total.
- Prompts carry no hex codes. The palette is held by one shared CSS grade.
final.style_block:
Macro photograph of a museum-quality architectural scale model, shot in a dark studio. One square diorama tile, a thick slab with crisp chamfered edges and sides painted matte deep navy, rests directly on a seamless matte navy model-maker's table that falls off into near-black. Locked camera, square-on to the model: centred, with no side rotation, looking down at about 38 degrees through a long telephoto lens, so the tile's sides barely converge and its front edge is perfectly level and parallel to the bottom of the frame. The tile spans almost the full width of the frame and sits in its lower two thirds; behind it there is only plain dark navy darkness. Tilt-shift depth of field: a sharp band from the street to the back of the plot; the tile's front face and the back ridge fall softly out of focus. Fixed layout, identical in every frame: a straight, empty, smooth pale-stone street crosses the front third of the tile from its left edge to its right edge, parallel to the front edge, with a low curb and a narrow sidewalk on each side. Behind the far sidewalk, in the middle of the tile and about half its width, lies the plot of a small shop in a quiet town of the Algerian high plateaus, framed by a low whitewashed boundary wall on each side. Beyond each wall stands the flat-roofed front of a neighbouring house in ochre and lime plaster with closed deep-navy wooden shutters, cut clean by the tile's edge. On the far sidewalk, in front of the right-hand house, one young street tree with a rounded clipped crown; in front of the left-hand house, one slim black wrought-iron street lamp. Along the back edge, a low jagged limestone ridge in layered grey-blue plaster: the Bibans mountains. Model-maker's materials: hand-sculpted plaster terrain dusted with fine ochre sand, lime-washed walls with a fine plaster texture, ochre limestone, basswood, tiny photo-etched brass details, static-grass tufts. Light: one warm brass-gold workshop lamp from high upper left, soft and directional, with long gentle shadows, a cool deep-navy ambient and a thin warm rim along the tile's top edges; the lamp itself is out of frame. Palette: ochre, whitewash, warm stone, aged brass and deep navy shadows. Calm, precise, quietly luxurious: one small object lit in a dark studio.

(The full block goes only into K0, the one text-to-image call. Every edit prompt states only the change, plus the short exclusion line. There are no hex codes in any prompt: the palette is enforced in code by one shared grade.)
final.negative_block:
Exclude: people, figurines, hands, animals and vehicles of any kind. No lettering anywhere: no text, letters, numbers, logos, signs or marks on any wall, paper, tape or screen. No glowing lines, neon, holograms, light trails, lens flare or sparkles. No glass cases, plinths or pedestals. No palm trees, domes, minarets or flags. No sky, sun or clouds. Not toy plastic, cartoon, clay or isometric; no fisheye, no tilted or angled view; no oversaturated colour.

Short form, closing every edit prompt: « No figures, hands, animals or vehicles; no lettering, numbers or marks anywhere; no glowing lines. » Add « no cab, no operator » to the crane frame. Add « completely blank » for the tape, the seal and the window glow.
final.road:
One straight horizontal coded line on every slide, at y_road = 1120 (held as one shared constant).

Position:
- Every render is normalised so its street centreline lands exactly on y 1120, so the line sits on the model street, inside the tilt-shift focus band.
- S1: starts at a brass benchmark ring at x 72 (nothing at the left edge) and leaves the right edge at y 1120.
- S2 to S8: enters at x 0 and leaves at x 1080, both at y 1120.
- S9: enters at y 1120 and ends at the terminus ring at x 420.

Parts on each slide:
- Two bridges, x 0–24 and x 1056–1080, always solid. Every seam therefore joins solid to solid at the same y, with no kink and no doubled dash, whatever the state.
- The tile run, x 24–1056 (S1: x 86–1056), carries the state's dash pattern. It uses pathLength=1000, periods that divide 1000 (20 and 50) and butt caps, so it starts on a dash and ends on a gap.

Strokes, bottom to top:
- halo: 12px #34d0e8 at .30, blurred 5px;
- core: #34d0e8, 3px in the chalk state and 4px after;
- hot centre: 1.5px #eaf1f8 at .6, in the lit state only.
This is the ceiling (README: no neon bloom). No wider spill, never behind or on type, no animation.

States (the progress meter that replaces numerals):
- S1–S2: chalk dots, dasharray 4 16.
- S3–S4: survey dashes, 12 8.
- S5: long dashes, 44 6, at .85 opacity for the light dip.
- S6–S9: solid and lit.

How it meets the image:
- The renders hold no line: every prompt excludes glowing lines and keeps the street empty, so the generator never fights the code.
- On each tile, a street spill: an ellipse 1000×56 centred on the line, radial #34d0e8 at .12 (.16 when lit) fading to 0, screen blend, clipped to the street band measured on K0.
- Under each bridge, a faint teal pool on the tabletop (ellipse 48×36, .14, blurred 10px), so the line reads as crossing the joint between two model tiles.
- On S6–S8, a coded ice-and-teal pool under the window brightens the line where the shop's light falls on the street.

Objects on it:
- The crate R1 rides it across the S3|S4 seam, base on y 1120.

Endpoints:
- S1 benchmark: 28px ring, 3px #e6b450 stroke, 6px #e6b450 dot.
- S9 terminus: 32px ring, 3px #e6b450 stroke, 8px dot, a 0 0 0 1px rgba(230,180,80,.45) ring. « LIEN EN BIO » sits at x 468, so the road ends on the pointer.

Fallback, if a chosen frame's street falls soft: halo to 14px, hot centre to .5.

prev.outcome (« Vous dites oui en connaissance de cause… ») is not used as a fallback: copy-library files it under Gate B and it makes the Aperçu explicit.
No 'rest' imagery anywhere: no annex, upper floor, roof frame or roof sketch. What follows a yes is undecided, so the owner switch changes copy only.

One constant workshop light from slide 1 to slide 8: no sun, sky, dusk or night. Only the shop's own lights switch on (the window on 6; the door, lantern and street lamp on 8), so nothing implies a one-day build. The neighbours stay shuttered.
The cover hook carries no time word and no product word: « bientôt » and the « vitrine »/site-vitrine pun are dropped, so the cover cannot borrow the site-vitrine lead time.

Step 2 uses the copy-library line with « D’abord » (from the facts bank's 'First with our questions'). The condition « dès que le cadrage est validé ensemble » sits on the same slide as « un prix ferme ». « Pas une fourchette, un chiffre » is left out. The wording is exact: « dès que », not « une fois »; « On construit », not « On bâtit ».

« 5 jours ouvrés » appears only with « à réception de vos contenus », on the same line as « Votre page d’accueil ». Slide 6 repeats « Votre page d’accueil » so the finished shop is not read as the whole site. The caption says the window stands for the homepage. No duration is summed anywhere.
Facts are said once (README › Spacing and layout). The caption does not retell the steps or the durations, and has no line listing the client's whole role (« À vous : décrire… » removed).

The content crates are closed and unmarked: no papers, framed pictures or labels. What the client supplies stays unsaid (claims.md §3). Building materials are no longer shown as the client's delivery.

The shop has no sign board and no plaque. The rendered window glow is blank, and the homepage is coded with no letters. « exemple » appears on every frame where the site shows (the loupe rim on 6, a chip with a leader on 7 and 8).

No light is drawn by the generator: the gold drawing, pen-tip spark, road, dimension lines, brackets and pools are all code. Every prompt excludes glowing lines. The words 'pen' and 'sketch' are gone from the prompts, and every call excludes hands.
The crane has no cab and no operator. The tape measure, the wax seal and the paper are blank; the tape's graduations are drawn in code inside the loupe, with no numerals.

Glow is capped to README's 'no neon bloom': the road halo is 12px at .30 with no wide spill; the drawing's glow is 10px at .35, on lines only; the wordmark block has no glow at scaled sizes. There is never a glow, gradient or shadow on type.

Local look: the palms are gone (they are rare on the high plateaus), replaced by a clipped street tree and a newly planted young olive. No domes, minarets, flags, zellige or souk. The owner approves K0 before the chain starts.
No hex codes in any generation prompt; the palette is held by one shared CSS grade. Edit prompts state only the change, plus a one-line exclusion.
No numbered kicker, page count, tile map, exit teaser or chevron. The kickers name who acts (À vous / À nous / À vous, puis à nous / Et après), and the road's dash states show progress.

French typography is specified per string: U+00A0 in « 24 h », « 5 jours » and « 30 min », before every « : » and inside « » ; typographic apostrophes. No ; ! ? sits on a visual (Geist Mono lacks U+202F, so the last kicker reads « Et après »). In the caption and alt texts: U+00A0 before « : » and U+202F before « ; ».

Every text block was measured with the shipped woff2 faces (HarfBuzz, kerning on) and ends above y 560. « On construit. » measures 1002px at 128px, so the cover runs at 120px (940px), inside the 972px measure.
The caption discloses « Images de synthèse » and the fictional shop. The renders are never called hand-made or real. Instagram's AI label is accepted, not stripped.
No URL, email, phone, handle or ref code on any visual. The end card says « Lien en bio ». The link goes out without the Aperçu share-card preview until Gate B (marketing.md › Link previews).
Never in the piece, caption or replies: « Aperçu », « gratuit », « free », « avant de payer », « 0 DA », « sans engagement », any price, or any call to action beyond « Lien en bio ».

The owner, and the lawyer already consulted on step 3, must clear this neutral telling before posting. If they refuse, slides 4, 6 and 7 need new copy; no rewording can fix it.

Generated images: claims.md rule 7, README › Imagery and claims.md §5 still forbid them. Generator habits: miniature scenes pull in tiny figures, crane operators, pseudo-letters on the seal, tape or window, and sometimes a pedestal under the tile. Every candidate is inspected at 200%; regenerate rather than retouch, above all on the cover.
A crisp coded road over a tilt-shift photo can look pasted on if the street falls outside the focus band. The fallback is ready: halo 14px, hot centre .5.

Even with « Votre page d’accueil » on slides 4 and 6 and the caption note, a reader may still take the finished shop to mean the whole site in 5 working days. The owner should read the sequence with that question in mind.

Layout depends on K1's measured geometry: the stair-cube top must land at y 660 or lower for the 440→620 fade and the slide 6 loupe. Otherwise move the fade to 400–580, shrink the loupe to Ø 300 and keep the text above y 540.

Design-system departures to record, so a later review does not 'fix' them back: word kickers with no number and no page count, the atlas loupe callout, generated renders, and the 9-slide length.

reviews.name: La table de maquette · Vous glissez. On construit.
strengths: Best cover of the three. The full finished shop stands on the empty plot as a crisp coded gold elevation, traced from the final frame, so in under a second the reader sees what will be built. The 132px hook « Vous glissez. On construit. » sets the rule of the game. « Glisser » means both 'swipe' and 'go smoothly', so the owner's message (smooth and easy) is in the hook itself.

The safest production plan. Renders never contain light lines (the negative block bans glowing lines), so every glow is in code: the ghost drawing, the road and the window homepage. That removes the main way the rejected 'random teal light ribbon' or sci-fi neon look could come back.

The frontal locked camera makes every overlay plain 2D: the homepage is a rectangle, and the brackets and dimension lines need no perspective maths. Coded 48px joints with brass joiner plates mean no render has to match another pixel for pixel at a seam. This is the only variant whose seams cannot break.
The drawing turns into the building. The same traced path runs at 100%, then .45, .35 and .30, and is finally replaced by real walls. This is the clearest visual proof that the world builds itself.

Good rhythm. The Vous/On headlines alternate (the reader's acts are tiny, the studio's are heavy). S4 is a headline-only breathing slide. S6 has a curiosity gap: the linen cloth is half slid off a dark window, a brass spotlight is aimed at it, and S7 pays it off with the lit window. On S7, the annex stakes rhyme with S2.
The tile fills almost the full slide width, so the build stays legible on a phone. Variant 1's band is about 780px wide; this one is 1032px.
A free second asset: the normalised frames play as stop-motion and give a 6–8 s Reel with no new generation. The coded end card with engraved Plate I ties the model to the brand's atlas.

Copy discipline is the best of the three. Step 2 is claims.md §1.4 word for word, with the scoping condition. « 5 jours ouvrés » never appears without « à réception de vos contenus ». The S7 fallback is prev.outcome, which is OK, with S7b/S8b frames ready.
fatal_flaws: The camera is frontal at 32° above the tabletop. That is the weakest angle for the miniature illusion: tilt-shift charm needs a higher view. The model may read as a dollhouse on a shelf rather than an exquisite tabletop world, which undercuts the owner's 'premium renders'.
The tile map (nine squares top right, the current one filled) is a page counter by another name. It brings back some of the UI chrome and progress-list feel the owner rejected.

S4's 'delivery' of crates plus cut stone plus timber beams makes « vos contenus » read as the client supplying building materials. That says the opposite of 'easy' and touches the undecided item of what the client supplies (claims.md §3).
The S5 text block is very likely to overflow. A 3-line 96px headline, 32px gap and 2-line 52px subline end around y 613, past the y 600 limit, where the image fade begins.
The ghost elevation is traced from S7 but overlaid on S5's half-built walls. Any drift between S5 and S7 will show as the drawing missing the walls, and S5→S6 is the riskiest edit.
Only one payoff relight (night). It is a weaker emotional landing than variant 1's dusk-then-night street coming alive.
fixes: Generate P0 candidates at about 38–40° (still frontal and symmetric) with stronger tilt-shift. Pick by phone-size thumbnail appeal, not only by levelness.
Replace the tile map with variant 1's kickers « À vous / À nous / Vous et nous », or drop it. Progress is already carried by the road and the build.
S4: show only the unmarked crates of blank papers and blank frames. Cut the stone stack and the timber. Let the coded brass parcels on the road carry the 'content in transit' idea.

S5: shorten the headline to « On construit. » (one line, 132px) and move « votre page d'accueil » into the subline (« Votre page d'accueil : 5 jours ouvrés à réception de vos contenus. »), so the block ends above y 600.
Draw the S5 ghost only on parts that are clearly unbuilt (parapet, rooftop cube), traced from S5's own registered walls, or drop it from S5.
Graft a dusk step, or variant 3's deliberate light dip on S5/S6 before the reveal, so the lit window lands harder.
Ship S7b/S8b (with prev.outcome) as the default, and switch to prev.tl5p and the annex only after the owner's written yes.

reviews.name: Ici, bientôt, votre vitrine (one plot, one camera)
strengths: The purest version of the direction the owner chose: one plot, one locked high three-quarter camera, every swipe a new state of the same model. It is true stop-motion, and the 3/4 tilt-shift view is the most premium-looking miniature of the three.

The cover headline is the wittiest line in the set. « Ici, bientôt, votre vitrine. » plays on the familiar construction hoarding sign and on « vitrine » as both shop window and « site vitrine », and it is aimed at the owner's own shop.
The kickers « À vous / À nous / Vous et nous » let the reader count their own small share. That is the cleanest way to prove 'easy' without claiming it.

The strongest payoff: S7 window on, S8 dusk with neighbours' windows, lamps, open door and glowing groove, S9 night with a lantern and a newly planted olive tree. The olive tree quietly rhymes with « Enraciné ».

Good seam craft. One y_A constant, dash periods that divide pathLength, a crate that straddles the S4|S5 seam as content in transit, and dash states (chalk, survey, long dash, solid) that work as a progress meter in place of numerals.

A rigorous anti-drift plan: P0 plate, 4 candidates, 50% onion-skin, 3-anchor registration with 6px residual, exposure matching. The window homepage is coded and mapped with matrix3d, labelled « exemple ».
fatal_flaws: The hero visuals are asked of the generator against its own negative block. S1's pen of light with sparks, S2's whole shop drawn in glowing teal lines in the air and S8's roof sketch are all requested in the render, while the negative block bans neon, holograms, sci-fi and light ribbons. The likely output is the holographic-neon look that echoes the rejected 'random teal light ribbon'. The SVG fallback covers only P2, not the cover (P1) or P8.

Too much on every slide: kicker, 2-line headline, 2-line subline, exit teaser, brass chevron, road, grid, two scrims, question pins, dimension lines, crate, chip. With the top 28% and bottom 18% reserved, the diorama is a roughly 780px band squeezed between text. It does not feel fast-paced.

The middle sags at phone size. S3 (stakes, a pennant, a tripod level) and S4 (strings, a trestle table, a wax seal) are tiny changes that will be mush on a phone. Two weak swipes in a row, in a 9-slide set.

The exit teasers (« Notre réponse → », « Le cadrage → », « Vos contenus → »...) chained across seven slides read as a table of contents, which brings back the list feel. With the chevron and the road there are three swipe cues per slide.
S9 crams the end card into the night render: headline, subline, chip, road terminus, « Lien en bio » and a three-part lockup. The final beat loses its calm.
fixes: Take every light drawing out of the renders. The camera is locked and frames are registered, so trace the finished P7 outline once in image space and reuse that SVG as the pen stroke on S1, the full sketch on S2 and the roof sketch on S8. It needs no perspective maths, and the glow stays in code (variant 2's method).
Cut the exit teasers, or keep one on S1 only, and drop the chevron. The kicker, the road and the crate carry the momentum.
Merge S3 and S4 into one 'reply + scope' slide (as variant 2 does) to free a slot. Use it for a clean coded end card, so S9 is just the night render with « On reste. ».
Raise the block to about 85% of frame width and shrink the reserved bands. Add a variant 3-style loupe on any slide whose key change is a small prop.
Default S8's subline to « La décision vous revient. » or prev.outcome until the owner confirms prev.tl5p in writing.
Drop « bientôt » if the owner reads it as a time promise. « Ici, votre vitrine. » keeps the pun.

reviews.name: La rue qui se bâtit (the Street Panorama)
strengths: The most entertaining individual set pieces in the set: a tailor's tape measure draped over the parapet for « sur mesure », a window wrapped in kraft paper that slides off at the reveal, and a deliberate light dip just before it.

Atlas-style loupe callouts, matching the brand's engraved-atlas world, make small details (the wax seal, the tape on the cornice) legible at phone size. This is the only variant that solves the small-prop problem.

Seamless half-objects on every seam (half palm, half crates, half scaffold, half lamp, half Timgad-like arch) are the strongest physical swipe cue, and the lit street lamp spills light in from the next slide.
Real Instagram know-how: slide 2 is built as a second cover because Instagram re-serves unswiped carousels from slide 2. The stage can be mirrored for an Arabic right-to-left version.
A smart way to hold geometry: generate the finished master first, then take it apart backwards. The light grows from left to right, so brightness itself pulls the eye.
fatal_flaws: It abandons the chosen direction. Mapping time onto space gives a street of seven copies of the same shop at different stages, which readers will see as seven different shops (the variant admits this). Swiping becomes walking down a street, not watching one world build itself, so 'you do nothing and it builds' is diluted.

A strict side-on elevation at rooftop height, 10° down, against a flat navy cyclorama with the mountains banned from the render, kills the tilt-shift miniature effect. It reads as a stage flat or dollhouse, not a premium diorama, and the facade is only about 550px wide on the slide.
The cover is overloaded. It carries the step-1 fact (« Vous décrivez le projet : deux minutes… ») under the hook, which spends the cover on information instead of the pure promise.

The heaviest and most fragile production: 7 lots, 6 background-removed cut-outs (palm fronds, scaffold lashings) and 2 detail shots, about 45 generations. It also relies on 300px feathered cross-fades between different renders' ground textures, which will smudge, and any change to the master invalidates the whole chain.
The window website is generated inside the render (lots 4–6), which risks gibberish UI. Variants 1 and 2 code it.

Copy drift: « une fois le cadrage validé ensemble » replaces the source's « dès que le cadrage est validé ensemble », and « On bâtit » replaces « on construit ». The brief allows facts only as written or shortened.
fixes: Fold its best devices (loupe, kraft-paper reveal, tape measure, light dip, half-object seams) into the one-plot model rather than shipping the panorama.
If the street is kept, raise the camera, restore the Bibans in the render, and lay one identical coded ghost silhouette over every lot so 'same shop, later' is unmistakable.
Make the cover pure hook and move step 1 to slide 2, which doubles as the second cover.
Code the window homepage and the cover thread outline. Keep the renders free of glow lines and UI.
Restore the exact wording: « dès que le cadrage est validé ensemble » and « On construit ».
Replace the cut-out set pieces with coded out-of-focus silhouettes on the seams to cut the generation count and the fringe artefacts.

Until the owner's written yes, set S8's subline to « La décision vous revient. », cut the « Si c'est oui… » caption line and remove the rooftop light sketch from P8 and P9, since what follows a yes is undecided.

reviews.name: La rue qui se bâtit (the Street Panorama)
strengths: Its visual metaphor is the most accurate on the scope of the 5 days. The ground floor and window (the homepage) finish at the presentation step, while the rooftop room ('le reste') stays a thread outline until later. The piece never implies the whole site is done in 5 working days.
Constant blue-hour stage light with no sun, clock or sky, explicitly so that the build cannot be read as 'built in one evening'. Durations appear one at a time and are never totalled.

The copy traces to listed facts. S2 keeps the scoping condition with the firm price (« une fois le cadrage validé ensemble », a faithful restatement in the site's price.estFine register), and S3 keeps « à réception de vos contenus » with « 5 jours ouvrés ».
« exemple » chips appear from the first frame where the website shows (S5) and are extended to the unwrapped sign on S6. The sign plate is blank apart from a plain circle.

The road glow is the most restrained (a 1px ring plus a 10px halo at 30%, never on type). The Bibans come from the brand's own engraving as a mask, not generated. The caption discloses that the images are generated and the shop is fictional.
fatal_flaws: The brief's French-typography hard rule is never specified. No coded layer sets U+00A0 in « 24 h ouvrées » (S2), « 5 jours ouvrés » and before the colon of « Votre page d'accueil : » (S3), before « : » in S1's subline (« le projet : deux minutes ») and S6's subline (« déjà faite : on enchaîne »), or inside « bonne chance » (S7). Nor does it set U+202F before « ; » in the caption (« vos contenus ; on construit »). With ordinary spaces, « 24 h » can wrap and colons can open a line.

The OWNER fallback circumvents the rule. If prev.tl5p is refused, the plan keeps S6's image of the roof frame going up under a crane and lets 'the image carry the yes'. That still states 'on enchaîne sur le reste', now as a picture, and what happens after a yes is undecided (business.md).

The website in the window is generated inside the master render (G1) and inherited by every later lot, rather than composited in code. It invites gibberish glyphs or pseudo-UI text on the fictional site, with only an after-the-fact fallback.
fixes: Add a typography spec to every coded layer and to export QA: U+00A0 in « 24 h », « 5 jours » and « 30 min », before every « : » and inside « » ; U+202F before ; ! ? (the caption's « contenus ; », « fictive, à titre d'exemple ; »).

Change the S6 fallback: if prev.tl5p is not confirmed in writing, render S6 without the roof frame or the crane and use « La décision vous revient. » or the headline alone. Remove the « Si c'est oui… » caption line.
Composite the window homepage in code (ice ground, navy bars, a brass button block, no letters) and render the glass as a blank glow in G1 to G3. Reject any render with visible glyphs.

Replace the date palms (P1, P6). They are Saharan and do not grow on the Bordj Bou Arréridj high plateaus, so they read as the postcard cliché the brief bans. Use olive trees, a ficus or a stone pillar.
P2 crates: closed and unmarked. Remove 'rolled papers and small blank picture frames', which depict what the client supplies (claims.md §3).
Add 'empty cab, no operator' to both crane prompts (G5, G2) and 'tape with no digits or printed marks' to the S4 and D4 prompts; inspect at 200%.
Add the link-preview caution to the risks: the bio link must not unfurl the site's Aperçu share card before Gate B (marketing.md › Link previews).
Keep the mirrored and tiled vista-far faint and away from type, or use the three Plate I layers unmirrored as variant 2 does, so the engraving is not visibly altered.

best_ideas_to_graft: From variant 1: split step 2 across two slides. S3 says « On revient sous 24 h ouvrées / D'abord avec nos questions »; S4 says « Un périmètre écrit. Un prix ferme. » with « Dès que le cadrage est validé ensemble. » on the same page. The firm price is never apart from its condition, and nobody reads 'price within 24 h'.

Use it in place of variant 2's prev.outcome (a Gate B Aperçu line) and variant 3's 'let the image carry the yes', and always remove the 'rest' imagery with it (rooftop sketch, annex, roof frame).

From variant 3: map the homepage to the finished ground floor and window, and 'le reste' to an upper room still drawn in thread. It is the only metaphor that does not imply the whole site is finished in 5 working days. Graft it only if prev.tl5p is confirmed; otherwise the upper room is simply part of the building.

From variant 2: a headline-only 'content' slide (« Vous envoyez vos contenus. ») with unmarked, closed crates, stone and timber. What the client supplies stays unsaid, unlike the crates of papers and framed pictures in variants 1 and 3.

From variant 2: a coded ghost elevation for the cover sketch instead of a generated 'pen of light'. There is no pen or freehand wording to invite a hand, and the drawing registers exactly with the finished shop.

From variant 1: a fully coded homepage in the window, mapped and clipped, with no letters and labelled « exemple » with a leader on every frame where it shows. Never generate UI inside the render, as variant 3 does.
From variant 3: the « exemple » chip extended to any visible sign plate or board. Graft it onto variant 2's S6 and variant 1's plaque frames.

From variants 1 and 2: explicit U+00A0/U+202F specs per string plus an export QA step, covering « 24 h », « 5 jours », « 30 min », colons, guillemets and the caption's ; and ?. Graft them into variant 3, which has none.
From variant 2: generate the fallback frames (no 'rest' imagery) in the same session as the main chain, so the piece can ship at once if the owner refuses prev.tl5p.

reviews.name: La table de maquette · Vous glissez. On construit.
strengths: Its camera is the only one of the three that works for both the generator and the coded layer. The view is square-on with a 32° downward tilt, so the street comes out as a level line. The road can then be one straight SVG at y 1120, and every overlay (the ghost elevation, the brackets, the dimension lines, the homepage in the window) is flat 2D with no matrix3d.

Its style block is the furthest from the generic AI look: « Macro photograph of a museum-grade physical architectural scale model », a chamfered tile painted navy, plaster dusted with ochre sand, basswood, photo-etched brass, static grass. That is real model-maker vocabulary. It pulls the generator toward photography and away from glossy CGI.
No light is asked of the generator: glowing lines are in the negative block, and all the teal is drawn in code. The rejected light ribbon and the hologram look cannot appear in the renders.

The seams are designed breaks. Each slide has a 48px coded joint, and the tabletop band, table edge, grid and road are drawn once on a 9720px strip. The renders never have to match pixel for pixel across a swipe. That is the honest answer to Canva's lack of outpainting.

The type stays in a fixed band (y 140–600) over the coded void and never sits on the picture. Normalisation is measurable and repeatable: front corners to x 24 and 1056, street to y 1120, a scale cap of 1.1, a rotation fix.

The cover is the most controllable hook: a photoreal empty plot with a crisp gold ghost elevation traced from the finished S7. On later slides the ghost fades (.45, .35, .30, then only the unbuilt parts), so the drawing literally becomes the building.

The Vous/On rhythm makes the client's part feel tiny. S4, with a headline and no subline, gives the sequence a breath. The S7b/S8b fallback frames for the OWNER line are made in the same session. S9 is coded only, with Plate I, so the model's ridge hands over to the brand atlas.
fatal_flaws: The payoff frames sit deepest in the chain. S7 is the 6th successive edit (reference 1 is always the previous stage) and S8 is the 7th. Softening, colour drift and object creep pile up on the reveal and the night beat. The accepted tolerances (street 8px; palm, lamp and ridge 15px) mean the promised stop-motion re-swipe will visibly jitter.

Every edit prompt repeats the whole style block and negative block word for word, about 3,500 characters. Re-describing the full scene in an edit call pushes the model to re-render the frame instead of preserving the reference, and it raises the truncation risk. The hex codes in the prompt are either ignored or printed as text.
S7 asks the generator to paint « a simple web page made only of abstract pale blocks » in the window. That invites gibberish UI and pseudo-letters underneath the coded homepage, and fights its edges.

The fixed top fade (0% above y 520, 100% from y 700) can cut the finished parapet, the rooftop stair-cube and the ridge once the shop is built. Generators do not reliably honour « the upper 45% is empty ».
fixes: Make the keyframes first. Generate S1 bare (text-to-image, 3–4 calls), then S7 finished and lit as one big edit of [S1] (3–4 calls). Then make the in-betweens from the nearer keyframe, with the other as the camera anchor: S2–S4 add to S1, S5–S6 strip back S7. No frame is more than 2 edits deep, and the payoff is depth 1. Make S8 (night) as a relight of S7, and S8b from S7b.

Composite a master plate on S1–S7. Outside a feathered polygon around the plot, every slide shows S1's own pixels: street, boundary walls, palm, lamp post, ridge, tile edges. Only the plot patch comes from each edit, registered on the four tile corners. The stop-motion then holds truly still and only the build moves. The rejection rate also drops, because drift outside the plot no longer matters.

Keep edit prompts to the change only, at most about 120 words: « Edit this photograph of a scale model. Change only the plot behind the far sidewalk: [delta]. Keep the camera, framing, tile, street, walls, palm, lamp post, ridge and lighting exactly as in the reference. No figures, no vehicles, no lettering anywhere. » Keep the full style block for S1 only.
S7 render: « the shop window glows with an even, blank, cool-white light, like a lit screen with nothing on it ». The coded homepage carries all the structure.

Remove every hex code from the prompts and use words instead (« one warm brass-gold workshop lamp », « deep navy shadows », « near-black background »). Enforce the palette in code with one shared grade: a CSS filter plus a low-opacity navy-to-brass gradient map, the same on every slide.

Generate the tile larger (about 95% of the width, about 70% of the height) for more detail, and shrink it into the coded void. Raise the fade to about y 430–620, then check on S6–S8 that the parapet and the rooftop cube sit below it.

At 14 × 22px the joiner plates come out about 5pt on a phone, so nobody sees them. Drop them and let the joint itself be the device: a 1px hairline-2 seam plus the teal bridge glow. Enlarge the tile-map squares to at least 28px or drop the map, since Instagram already shows the dots.
Add V1's pen-tip spark at one end of the cover's gold ghost (an 18px radial, screen blend), so it reads as being drawn now rather than as a static blueprint.
For a high-plains town, consider a young olive or a pruned street ficus instead of the palm. Palms are allowed by the brief, so confirm with the owner.

reviews.name: Ici, bientôt, votre vitrine (one plot, one camera)
strengths: It has the best copy idea of the three. « Ici, bientôt, votre vitrine. » plays on « vitrine » as both the shop window and the « site vitrine », which an Algerian small-business owner reads in one second.
The kickers « À vous / À nous / Vous et nous » let the reader count their own small part. That proves the ease without claiming it, and replaces the numbering elegantly.

The road-line states (chalk dots, survey dashes, long dashes, then solid and lit) form a progress meter with no numerals. The dash maths is correct: pathLength 1000, periods that divide 1000 and butt caps guarantee a clean phase at every seam.
The R1 crate straddling the S4|S5 seam (your content in transit, dragged across by your own thumb) is the most entertaining seam mechanic of the three.

It has the most rigorous QA: an unpublished P0 master plate, a 50% onion-skin test, three-anchor registration with 6px or less residual, per-slide exposure matching, inspection at 200%, and a 9720px contact strip.
It splits the window correctly: the render shows a blank light panel, and the homepage is composited in code, so no generated UI ever appears.
Its local choices are the most authentic: an olive tree, no palms at that altitude, lime render, navy shutters. The dusk-to-night relight gives an emotional close.
fatal_flaws: The hero is too small. The plot is about a third of a block that fills 72% of the width, so the shop is roughly 250–300px wide on the 1080 slide and its arched window about 120–150px. The 800×600 coded homepage, the whole payoff, shrinks to a smudge of about 50pt on a phone.

P1 and P2 ask the generator for the very things the negative block bans (« glowing lines », « holographic », « neon », sparks). On a contradictory prompt, the likeliest output for a full building drawn in light lines in the air is a Tron or hologram wireframe: the rejected sci-fi look, and on slide 2, which Instagram re-serves as a second cover.

The chain runs forward, P0 → P1 → … → P9, and adds P0 only after drift appears. The payoff frames P7–P9 are 7 to 9 edits deep, so softening and colour cast land on the most important images. The registration transform corrects translation and scale, but not neighbours whose windows have been redrawn.

A cut block of earth with visible soil strata, floating in a navy void, is the most common AI diorama trope (the floating isometric island). It reproduces the generic AI-render feel the owner rejected, only with a different subject.

The camera is turned slightly and the block fills only 72% of the width. To reach the seams, the coded road has to leave the model and cross empty void at street height. That segment is a glowing line floating in space, which is exactly a light ribbon.

It counts on the generator to leave exact 28% and 18% empty bands. Generators ignore percentage layouts, so the Bibans and the tabletop will often sit inside the type bands. The 120px two-line cover headline already fills the 378px band exactly.
fixes: Camera: zero yaw, square-on, a 38–40° downward tilt, a long lens. Let the earth base run past both frame edges, so the street crosses from x 0 to x 1080 exactly level inside the model and the road never crosses the void. Make the lot 45–50% of the frame width, with the neighbours as partial slices at the edges.
Replace the floating strata block with a museum model base: « a dark-navy painted model baseboard with a thin cut edge of layered earth, on a model-maker's table » (borrow V2's materials vocabulary).

Make the keyframes first. P0 bare is text-to-image. P7 (finished, window lit blank) is one edit of [P0]. P3–P6 are edits of whichever keyframe is closer, with both as imageReferences. P8 (dusk) and P9 (night) are both relights of P7, not of each other. Nothing goes deeper than 2 edits.

Composite a master plate. On S1–S7, everything outside a feathered mask around the lot (neighbours, lamps, street, ridge) comes from P0's pixels, and only the lot comes from each edit. Neighbours and mountains can then never flicker, and the 3-anchor registration is needed only for the patch.

Never render light. P1 shows a physical surveyor's chalk line or taut string on the soil, and P2 shows only stakes. Draw the pen stroke, pen tip and perspective sketch in code, traced from the chosen P7 so the sketch is the real building. Make this the primary route, not the fallback.

Keep edit prompts to the change only, at most about 120 words, with no style block and no hex codes: « Edit this photograph of a scale model. Change only the lot: … Everything else stays exactly as in the reference. No figures, no lettering. »

Generate the model filling about 85% of the frame, then place it at 85–90% over a coded #0a1420 void with a feathered radial mask. Let the code create the type bands rather than asking the generator for them.
S7 payoff: add an atlas loupe (V3's device), 360–420px across, with the coded homepage flat inside, a 1px hairline-2 leader to the window, and « exemple » on the loupe.

Lighten each page: keep the kickers, and drop either the exit teasers or the question pins. Bring S4 back to 96px or more by shortening to « Périmètre écrit. / Prix ferme. », with the scoping condition still on the same page. Budget honestly: 10 frames × 4 calls plus R1 and re-rolls is closer to 55 calls than 40.

reviews.name: La rue qui se bâtit (the Street Panorama)
strengths: It has the most entertaining beats of the three: a window wrapped in kraft paper as a curiosity gap, the light deliberately dipping before the reveal, a tailor's tape measure draped over the parapet for « sur mesure », a wax-sealed sheet for the firm price, the open door, and lights growing from left to right.
It generates the finished, fully lit shop first, as a clean text-to-image keyframe, and that silhouette drives every earlier lot. That is the right instinct: the payoff is never degraded.

It builds one 8640 × 1350 stage, so everything that crosses a seam is drawn once and continuous by construction. The plinth with a model-maker's tick scale and the station nodes are classy, on-brand replacements for kickers and page counts.
Its atlas-style loupe callouts (a ring, brass ticks, a leader line) change the scale and show small details at phone size. It is the best single device in the three plans.
The type sits on clean zones, the empty backdrop above and the coded plinth below the curb, never over the picture. Slide 2 is built to work as a second cover.
Two extras come free: a constant-speed pan of the stage makes a tracking-shot Reel, and a mirrored stage gives the right-to-left order for a future Arabic version.
fatal_flaws: A strict side-on view at 10° down kills the miniature. Tilt-shift only reads as a tabletop model from a high angle. At 10°, in front of a seamless cyclorama, each lot reads as a stage-set facade or a real building at blue hour. The diorama magic the owner chose is lost.

A continuous street of seven lots shows seven different shops side by side, which contradicts the story of one plot over time. The headlines have to correct what the image says, and the variant's own risk list admits it.
The cover is G7, the deepest generation in the backward chain (6 edits from the master). The frame that has to stop the scroll is the most degraded.

The production load is the heaviest: 7 lots, 6 cut-out seam pieces and 2 loupe details, so 15 accepted images and 45 or more calls. Canva's background remover on navy-on-navy palm fronds and scaffold lashings (dark subject, dark background, low contrast) will chew the edges, and every seam then falls back to a coded silhouette.
The 300px cross-fades mix two different pavement renders at the curb, exactly where the road runs, so they ghost: doubled setts and doubled curb edges.
White-line engraving art (vista-far.webp as a luminance mask) sits directly behind photoreal model renders. Two incompatible image languages share one depth stack.
The cover is overloaded: a 120px hook, a three-line step-1 subline and the wordmark. The hook loses its one-second read.
fixes: Tilt the camera to 25–30° down and keep zero yaw. Tilting alone keeps every street-parallel line level, so the curb and the road stay perfectly horizontal while the roofs and the street surface show and the tilt-shift miniature reads again.
Build every lot from the master: each one is an edit of G1, with the neighbouring lot only as a second reference for props. Make the cover from [G1] directly. No frame deeper than 2.

Use one shared ground strip. Cut the master's pavement and curb band once and tile or extend it across the whole stage in code, and mask each lot above the pavement line. Cross-fade only the bare ground and the backdrop, never the setts or the curb where the road runs.

Generate the seam pieces on a flat mid-grey seamless background with the same key light, remove the background, then grade them to the blue-hour look in code. Prefer solid shapes (lamp, arch, crates) over palms, or make the coded out-of-focus foreground silhouette the primary route.

Make 'same shop, later' unmistakable. Composite each lot's unchanged parts from the master's pixels, and lay V2's coded ghost elevation over the unbuilt parts. Or drop the continuous street for separate modules joined by coded joints, as in V2.
Move step 1 off the cover. The cover holds the hook and a one-line swipe promise only; step 1 opens slide 2 (9 slides is still within the brief).
Keep Plate I off the stage behind the model. Use it only on the end card, or as a very faint band explicitly framed as a printed backdrop.
Generators almost always print digits on a tape measure. Ask for « a plain golden tape with no markings », draw the ticks in code inside the D4 loupe, and reject any render with glyphs at 200%.

best_ideas_to_graft: Camera: use V2's square-on view with zero yaw, but tilted about 35–40° down to keep V1's miniature feel. Tilting keeps the street exactly level, so a single straight coded road and flat 2D overlays work; turning the camera breaks both.

Keyframes first (V3's instinct, applied to V1 and V2): generate the bare plate (text-to-image) and the finished lit shop (one edit of the plate) before anything else. Make each in-between from the nearer keyframe with the other as the camera reference. No frame goes deeper than 2 edits; the cover is depth 0 and the payoff depth 1.

Master-plate patch compositing (new): on every daytime slide, everything outside a feathered mask around the plot is the master plate's own pixels, and only the plot comes from each edit. This removes drift on neighbours, trees and the ridge, makes V2's stop-motion re-swipe genuinely static, and cuts the rejection rate.

No light in renders (V2): the generator draws only physical things (stakes, string, chalk, crates). Every teal line, ghost drawing, pen tip and glow is coded and traced from the finished keyframe. This removes the hologram and light-ribbon risk.
V2's gold ghost elevation, traced from the finished shop and fading to only the unbuilt parts as walls rise, plus V1's pen-tip spark on the cover so it reads as being drawn now.

V1's hook « Ici, bientôt, votre vitrine. » (shop window plus « site vitrine ») is the strongest line. A/B it against V2 and V3's « Vous glissez. On construit. », or use one as the cover and the other as slide 2's second cover.
V1's kickers « À vous / À nous / Vous et nous » and its road-line states (dots, dashes, long dashes, solid and lit) as a progress meter with no numerals.
V3's atlas loupe callout for the payoff: a 360–420px ring with brass ticks and a leader to the window, holding the coded homepage flat at a legible size, labelled « exemple ».

V3's story beats for entertainment: the window wrapped in kraft paper with a light dip just before the reveal, a tailor's tape for « sur mesure » (blank tape, ticks in code), and a wax-sealed sheet for the written scope and firm price.
Seam mechanics for « Vous envoyez »: V1's crate riding the seam (dragged across by the thumb) or V2's brass parcels gliding along the road. Pick one, not both.

Prompt hygiene: edit prompts that state only the change, in about 120 words or fewer, with no repeated style block. No hex codes anywhere: use colour words and enforce the palette with one shared code grade. A short exclusion line (« an empty model: no figures, no vehicles, no lettering anywhere ») instead of long lists naming pedestals, light bulbs or camels the scene never invites.
Let code own the layout space: generate the model large for detail, then shrink it into a coded navy void with feathered masks. Never ask the generator for 'top 28% empty'.

QA stack: V1's onion-skin rejection, three-anchor registration and per-slide exposure matching, V2's normalisation with its scale cap, and V3's shared ground strip so no two pavement renders are ever cross-faded.
Cut-outs (V1's crate, V3's seam pieces): generate them on a flat mid-grey background, then remove the background and grade. Never navy on navy, where the remover fails.

Pilot before production, once the owner allows generation (the user's current instruction is planning only, no generating yet): three Canva calls (bare plate, one additive edit, one subtractive edit), onion-skinned against the plate to measure how faithful imageReferences editing really is. If neighbours redraw or the drift is over 15px, go fully to patch compositing. Each call returns one image, so '4 candidates' means 4 calls: budget about 30 calls for a V2-style build.

Endings: V2's coded end card with Plate I (the model's ridge becomes the engraved atlas), V3's plinth with a model-maker's tick scale, and V1's dusk-to-night relight. Both night frames are relights of the finished keyframe, not of each other.
